name: AMC3336DWER
title: Reinforced isolated ±1 V delta-sigma modulator, self-powered high side
summary: The AMC3336 is a second-order delta-sigma modulator with a ±1 V differential input and 1 GΩ input resistance, built for voltage sensing behind high-ohm dividers. Its bitstream crosses a reinforced capacitive barrier (6000 VPK, 1.2 kVRMS working) to a low side clocked externally at 9 to 21 MHz. An on-chip isolated DC/DC converter makes the high-side supply from one 3.3 V or 5 V rail on the low side, and an open-drain DIAG pin flags missing or invalid data. With a sinc3 filter at OSR = 256 it gives 16 bits at 78 kSPS.

circuits.title: Grid-side voltage and current sensing in a solar inverter
circuits.description: One phase of a solar inverter feeds the grid through an LCL filter (L2, CF, L1) and a relay (SW1, SW2). Neither sensing point has a local supply, so both isolated parts make their own high-side supply from the 3.3 V or 5 V low-side rail. The AMC3336 (U1) reads the line-to-neutral voltage across RL1SNS, the sense resistor in a string RL11, RL1SNS, RL12 from L1 to N, with 1 nF across its inputs; its INN and HGND sit on the sense resistor's lower end. An AMC3306M05 (U2) reads the phase current across RSHUNT on the grid side of the filter, through 10 Ω resistors and 10 nF across its inputs, its HGND on the relay end of the shunt. Each part has the same supply decoupling: 1 µF and 1 nF on DCDC_OUT, which feeds HLDO_IN, 100 nF on HLDO_IN, 1 nF and 100 nF on HLDO_OUT, 100 nF on DCDC_IN tied to LDO_OUT, 1 nF and 1 µF on VDD, and 47 kΩ pulling DIAG up to VDD. CLKIN comes from the microcontroller, DOUT goes to it, and DIAG optionally does.

parts.value: inverter phase leg: high- and low-side switches with gate drivers, bidirectional switch to the DC-link midpoint

notes: The resistor string values for 120 VRMS and 230 VRMS lines are in the resistor value examples table.

circuits.title: Input filter on a resistive divider
circuits.description: With a high-impedance divider ahead of the device, one 1 nF capacitor across INP and INN filters the input. R1, RSNS and R2 form the divider, RSNS spans the inputs, and INN is tied to HGND.
notes: The supply, ground and digital pins connect as in the decoupling circuit.

circuits.title: Decoupling
circuits.description: The device runs from one 3.3 V or 5 V supply on VDD; its own DC/DC converter makes the high-side supply. On the low side C8 (1 nF) sits right at VDD with C9 (1 µF) behind it, and C4 (100 nF) decouples DCDC_IN, which is tied to LDO_OUT, against DCDC_GND. On the high side C2 (1 µF) and C3 (1 nF) decouple DCDC_OUT, which feeds HLDO_IN; C1 (100 nF) also sits on HLDO_IN. C6 (1 nF) and C5 (100 nF) decouple HLDO_OUT. A resistor string RL11, RL1SNS, RL12 scales the line voltage; the drop across RL1SNS drives INP and INN, C10 (1 nF) filters it, and INN, HGND and DCDC_HGND are joined at the pins. R1 (47 kΩ) pulls the open-drain DIAG up to VDD.
notes: C8, C3, C6 and C4 go as close to the device as possible.

operation.text: Decimated with a sinc3 filter at OSR = 256, the bitstream gives 16 bits with 85 dB dynamic range at 78 kSPS. The input is one differential channel, ±1 V full scale, with 1 GΩ typical input resistance; the barrier is reinforced capacitive isolation with a 1.2 kVRMS working voltage, certified to VDE V 0884-11 and UL1577. It is specified from –40 °C to +125 °C and meets CISPR-11 and CISPR-25 emission limits.

A differential input buffer drives a second-order delta-sigma modulator on the high side. Its 1-bit output crosses the barrier and leaves at DOUT, clocked by the external CLKIN, so several channels can share one clock. The data path crosses a double silicon-dioxide capacitive barrier; power crosses through an on-chip transformer insulated by a thin polymer film.

The input stage is high impedance and low bias current, suited to high-ohm dividers. Its buffer is chopper-stabilized at fCLKIN / 32, which shows as a spur at 625 kHz with a 20 MHz clock. Beyond the absolute maximum input range the ESD diodes conduct and input current must stay below 10 mA. Linearity and noise hold only inside VFSR and the operating common-mode range VCM.

A switched-capacitor, feed-forward, second-order loop: the input minus the 1-bit DAC output feeds two integrators in series; a comparator decides each clock which way the DAC steps, so the average of the output follows the input. Quantization noise is pushed to high frequencies, so a digital low-pass filter after the device both improves performance and decimates the 1-bit stream into wider words at a lower rate. C2000 and Sitara microcontrollers carry such a filter (SDFM); an FPGA or CPLD can also do it.
On-off keying: a one is sent as bursts of a high-frequency carrier, nominally 480 MHz, a zero as no carrier.

0 V in gives ones 50% of the time; +1 V gives 90% (ideal 16-bit code 58982); –1 V gives 10% (code 6553). Past ±1 V the output turns nonlinear as quantization noise rises, and at or beyond ±1.25 V it clips to all zeros or all ones, except that one opposite bit appears every 128 clocks, so a real full-scale input can be told from a lost high-side supply.
If the DC/DC output drops below its undervoltage threshold, DOUT holds a constant stream of zeros.

A low-side LDO steadies VDD for a full-bridge driver; an air-core laminate transformer, immune to magnetic fields, passes power to a high-side full-bridge rectifier and a high-side LDO. The low-side LDO's output is not a constant voltage and drives no external load. The high-side LDO is regulated and can source up to IH (1 mA) extra for a small auxiliary circuit such as a preamplifier, active filter or comparator; IH holds to 85 °C ambient and falls linearly above it. The converter uses a spread-spectrum clock to cut radiated emissions, and its resonator is synchronized to the modulator.

DIAG is open drain. It is held low at power-up until the high side is in regulation and data flow. It is pulled low again if the low side stops receiving data from the high side, or if DCDC_OUT or HLDO_OUT drops below its undervoltage threshold; in both cases DOUT stays low.

The digital interface and DIAG work once VDD passes VDDPOR; analog functions, the high side included, start once VDD passes VDDUV. Going down, analog stops below VDDUV (falling) and the digital side below VDDPOR (falling). Below VDDPOR the digital outputs are high impedance, clamped one diode drop above VDD.
A sinc3 filter is the smallest that gets the best from a second-order modulator. Characterization uses sinc3, OSR = 256 and 16-bit output words unless a condition says otherwise.

230 VRMS example: 100 µA through the divider at the 360 V peak sets about 3.6 MΩ in total. At 75 V per resistor the top and bottom strings need at least 360 / 75 = 5 unit resistors of 3.6 MΩ / 5 = 720 kΩ, taken as 715 kΩ (E96). RL1SNS is sized so the peak line gives +1 V across it: 10 kΩ. The 120 VRMS case is worked the same way.

An RC filter ahead of the input improves SNR. Its corner should be at least ten times below fCLKIN, its DC resistance should not drop much voltage, and both inputs should see equal source impedance. Behind a high-impedance divider a single capacitor across the inputs is enough.

C2000 and Sitara microcontrollers have up to eight hardwired filter channels, each with a precise path for control and a fast path for overcurrent detection. A delta-sigma filter calculator helps pick OSR and filter order for a wanted resolution and response time.

Inputs must not float while powered: with both open the bitstream is undefined. INN needs a DC path to HGND, direct or through a resistor, and the common-mode range must be kept. Load the high-side LDO no more than IH, minding its derating at high temperature. LDO_OUT, the low-side LDO output, takes no external load.

VDD is 3.3 V or 5 V nominal. Place a low-ESR 1 nF capacitor right at VDD, then 1 µF. Decouple DCDC_IN to DCDC_GND with a low-ESR 100 nF close to the device. On the high side use 1 µF plus a low-ESR 1 nF as close as possible across DCDC_OUT and DCDC_HGND, and for the high-side LDO a low-ESR 1 nF as close as possible, then 100 nF. HGND comes from the end of the sense resistor on INN; INN and HGND, and DCDC_HGND and HGND, may be joined right at the pins. Ceramic capacitors lose much of their value under DC bias, more so in low-profile cases; size them for the effective capacitance at their working voltage.

Each decoupling capacitor sits next to its supply pin, as near as it can. The sense resistor goes close to INP and INN, with the two connections laid out symmetrically. The area under the device across the barrier is kept clear of all copper and other conductors. This layout, used on the evaluation module, meets CISPR-11 radiated-emission limits.

All four orderable numbers are the same SOIC-16 (DWE) part on 2000-piece reels, marked AMC3336, rated -40 to 85 °C operating temperature, MSL 3 at 260 °C peak. An automotive version, AMC3336-Q1, also exists.

Two land patterns: IPC-7351 nominal, 16 pads of (2) × (0.6) mm on (1.27) pitch with (9.3) mm row span, giving 7.3 mm clearance and creepage; and a high-voltage option with (1.65) × (0.6) mm pads and (9.75) mm row span, giving 8.1 mm. Solder mask opens 0.07 mm all round (non-solder-mask-defined) or overlaps the metal by 0.07 mm minimum (solder-mask-defined). The stencil is 0.125 mm thick with the same apertures.
